rationale:
The supplied proof has two substantive steps. They are mathematically independent, use disjoint toolkits, and are each a standard, reusable fact. Each becomes one child.
(1) tangent_le_plane is supplied step 2, generalized to an arbitrary subspace V: if a − x ∈ V for all a ∈ A, then every approximate tangent plane of A at x lies in V. This is measure theory: a C_c bump vanishing on V, zero blow-up integrals, the approximate-tangent limit, and support(Hⁿ⌞Q) = Q.
(2) frame_sign is supplied step 4 as pure multilinear algebra: two orthonormal frames τ, e with the same span satisfy α(τ) = c·α(e) for every n-covector α, with one constant c ∈ {±1}. The tools are eq_smul_basis_det and the ±1 change-of-basis determinant between orthonormal bases.

How the children imply the selected statement (supplied steps 1, 3, 5 stay in the parent):
- e_j := EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 is orthonormal (EuclideanSpace.orthonormal_single composed with ι, which is injective because StrictMono).
- Put V := span(range e). Every v with v_i = 0 for all i ∉ range ι lies in V: expand v = Σ_i v_i e_i; terms with i ∈ range ι lie in V and the others vanish. Hence a − x ∈ V for all a ∈ A, because (a − x)_i = a_i − x_i = 0 off range ι.
- tangent_le_plane gives Q ≤ V.
- finrank Q = n (first component of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt) and finrank V = n (finrank_span_eq_card), so Q = V (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq).
- Unpacking IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q gives an orthonormal τ with span(range τ) = Q = span(range e) and a sign σ with ξ α = σ·α τ.
- frame_sign gives α τ = ±α e uniformly in α. The four sign combinations give the dichotomy; n = 0 is covered uniformly.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of a set lying in an affine plane x + V are contained in V
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, A ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P), x ∈ ℝ^P, and let Q, V be linear subspaces of ℝ^P. Assume a − x ∈ V for every a ∈ A.

Assume also that Q is an approximate tangent space of A at x in the sense of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4). This means:
- finrank Q = n, and
- for every compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺.
Here η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) is blowUpMap x r, Hⁿ = μHE[n], each integral is taken against the restriction of Hⁿ to the indicated set, and no measurability of A is assumed.

Then Q ⊆ V.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), (∀ a ∈ A, a - x ∈ V) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q → Q ≤ V
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the bump-function argument), stated for an arbitrary subspace V. Compare Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 and the test-function argument of Remark 1.5(3), book/chapter-03.txt lines 76–91.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For r ∈ ℝ, η_r := blowUpMap x r, so η_r(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x), and S_r := η_r(A) = blowUpMap x r '' A. Let μ := Hⁿ⌞Q = μHE[n].restrict Q.

1. Blow-ups lie in V. Let r ∈ ℝ and a ∈ A. By hypothesis a − x ∈ V, and V is closed under scalar multiplication, so η_r(a) = r⁻¹ • (a − x) ∈ V. Hence S_r ⊆ V for every r ∈ ℝ.

2. Set-up of a contradiction. Let q ∈ Q and suppose q ∉ V. The subspace V of the finite-dimensional normed space ℝ^P is closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and nonempty (0 ∈ V). Hence d := infDist(q, V) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos).

3. A bump function. Define g : ℝ^P → ℝ by g(y) := max(0, d/2 − dist(y, q)).
 (i) g is continuous, as a max of continuous functions.
 (ii) g(y) ≥ 0 for every y.
 (iii) support g = ball(q, d/2), because max(0, t) ≠ 0 iff t > 0, and d/2 − dist(y, q) > 0 iff dist(y, q) < d/2.
 (iv) g has compact support. If y ∉ closedBall(q, d/2), then dist(y, q) > d/2, so g(y) = 0. Closed balls of ℝ^P are compact (HasCompactSupport.intro with isCompact_closedBall).
 Therefore g underlies an element f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), a CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ⟨⟨g, continuity⟩, compact support⟩, with f(y) = g(y) for all y.

4. g vanishes on V. Let v ∈ V. Then d = infDist(q, V) ≤ dist(q, v) = dist(v, q) (infDist_le_dist_of_mem). So d/2 − dist(v, q) ≤ −d/2 < 0, and g(v) = 0.

5. The blow-up integrals vanish. Fix r ∈ ℝ. Every point of S_r lies in V by step 1, and f = g vanishes on V by step 4, so f(y) = 0 for every y ∈ S_r. Hence ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
 No measurability of S_r is needed. The set O := {f ≠ 0} is open, hence Borel, and (Hⁿ⌞S_r)(O) = Hⁿ(O ∩ S_r) = Hⁿ(∅) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply for the measurable set O). So f = 0 holds Hⁿ⌞S_r-almost everywhere.

6. The limit plane integral is zero. Apply the second component of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q to f: the function r ↦ ∫_{S_r} f dHⁿ tends to ∫_Q f dHⁿ along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. By step 5 this function is identically 0, so it also tends to 0 along 𝓝[>] 0. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial and ℝ is Hausdorff, so limits are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique). Hence ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0.

7. The plane measure charges every ball around q. The first component of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q gives finrank Q = n. Hence the support of μ = Hⁿ⌞Q equals Q (support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, SimonGMT Ch. 3, Rectifiable.lean). Since q ∈ Q, q lies in the support of μ, so every neighbourhood of q has positive μ-measure (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall). Because d/2 > 0, ball(q, d/2) is a neighbourhood of q, so μ(ball(q, d/2)) > 0.

8. Integrability. Since finrank Q = n, μ is a regular measure (regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), and in particular it is finite on compact sets. A continuous function with compact support is integrable for such a measure (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). So g is μ-integrable.

9. Positivity and contradiction. Since g ≥ 0 and g is μ-integrable, integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg gives 0 < ∫ g dμ ⟺ 0 < μ(support g). By step 3(iii) and step 7, μ(support g) = μ(ball(q, d/2)) > 0, so ∫ g dμ > 0. But the set integral ∫_Q f dHⁿ is by definition ∫ g dμ, and it is 0 by step 6. Contradiction.

10. Therefore every q ∈ Q lies in V, that is, Q ≤ V. The argument is uniform in n; for n = 0, Q = {0} ⊆ V in any case. ∎
proof_key_steps: Every blow-up blowUpMap x r '' A = {r⁻¹(a − x) : a ∈ A} lies in V, because a − x ∈ V and V is a subspace.
If q ∈ Q \ V, then d := infDist(q, V) > 0. The bump g = max(0, d/2 − dist(·, q)) is in C_c, is nonnegative, has support ball(q, d/2), and vanishes on V.
Every blow-up integral of g is 0 (g vanishes pointwise on the blow-up; no measurability is needed). The approximate-tangent limit and uniqueness of limits along 𝓝[>] 0 give ∫_Q g dHⁿ = 0.
Since finrank Q = n, supp(Hⁿ⌞Q) = Q and Hⁿ⌞Q is regular. So g is integrable, μ(ball(q, d/2)) > 0, and integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg gives ∫_Q g dHⁿ > 0. This contradiction shows Q ≤ V.

subproblems.title: Orthonormal frames with the same span evaluate all n-covectors equally up to one global sign
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ, e : Fin n → ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be orthonormal families (for the Euclidean inner product) with span(range τ) = span(range e). Then one of the following holds:
- α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = α(e_0, …, e_{n−1}) for every n-covector α, or
- α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = −α(e_0, …, e_{n−1}) for every n-covector α.
Here an n-covector is a continuous alternating n-linear map α : (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ, that is, an element of Covector (Euclid P) n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ e : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Orthonormal ℝ e → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range e) → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α τ = α e) ∨ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α τ = -α e)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof, isolated as a statement about two orthonormal frames of the same subspace. Compare Simon Ch. 6, §1 and §3: an n-plane is oriented by ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ for any orthonormal basis τ of it (book/chapter-06.txt lines 2224–2226).

Notation. An n-covector is α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ. α(v) denotes its value on v : Fin n → ℝ^P. Let W := span(range e) ⊆ ℝ^P.

1. A basis of W from e. Since e is orthonormal, it is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent). Hence b := Basis.span of this linear independence is a basis of W indexed by Fin n, with (b j : ℝ^P) = e j for every j (Basis.coe_span_apply). Consequently finrank W = n (finrank_span_eq_card and Fintype.card (Fin n) = n).

2. τ as a family in W. For each j, τ j ∈ span(range τ) = W by hypothesis. Let τ_W : Fin n → W be τ_W j := ⟨τ j, _⟩, so (τ_W j : ℝ^P) = τ j.

3. Reduction to one determinant. Fix an n-covector α. Let α_W be the alternating n-linear map W^n → ℝ obtained by composing the underlying alternating map of α with the inclusion W.subtype (AlternatingMap.compLinearMap). Thus α_W(w_0, …, w_{n−1}) = α(w_0, …, w_{n−1}).
 Since b is a basis of W indexed by the same type Fin n, AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det gives α_W = α_W(b) • det_b, where det_b is the determinant alternating map of b. Evaluating at τ_W:
 α(τ) = α_W(τ_W) = α_W(b) · det_b(τ_W) = α(e) · c, where c := det_b(τ_W) ∈ ℝ.
 Here α_W(b) = α(e) because (b j : ℝ^P) = e j, and α_W(τ_W) = α(τ) because (τ_W j : ℝ^P) = τ j. The number c depends only on b and τ_W, not on α.

4. c = ±1. The inner product of W is the restriction of that of ℝ^P (Submodule.coe_inner). So the orthonormality of e and τ in ℝ^P transfers verbatim: b and τ_W are orthonormal families in W.
 (i) b is an orthonormal basis: oe := b.toOrthonormalBasis, with oe.toBasis = b (Basis.toBasis_toOrthonormalBasis).
 (ii) τ_W is orthonormal, hence linearly independent, and has n = finrank W members, so span(range τ_W) = W (LinearIndependent.span_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank'). Thus oτ := OrthonormalBasis.mk is an orthonormal basis of W with ⇑oτ = τ_W (OrthonormalBasis.coe_mk).
 (iii) The change-of-basis determinant between two orthonormal bases of a finite-dimensional real inner product space is ±1. Its matrix is orthogonal, so the determinant squares to 1 (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real: oe.toBasis.det oτ = 1 ∨ oe.toBasis.det oτ = −1).
 By (i) and (ii), oe.toBasis.det oτ = det_b(τ_W) = c, so c = 1 or c = −1.

5. Conclusion. If c = 1, step 3 gives α(τ) = α(e) for every n-covector α. If c = −1, step 3 gives α(τ) = −α(e) for every n-covector α. Since c does not depend on α, this is the required dichotomy.

6. The case n = 0 is included. Then W = {0}, b and τ_W are the empty family, and det_b(τ_W) = 1 (the determinant of the empty matrix), so the first alternative holds. The argument above covers this case without change. ∎
proof_key_steps: W := span(range e) has the basis b = Basis.span (e linearly independent) with b_j = e_j, and finrank W = n. Each τ_j lies in span(range τ) = W.
For each n-covector α, restrict it to W and apply AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det with the basis b. This gives α(τ) = det_b(τ_W) · α(e), where c := det_b(τ_W) does not depend on α.
b and τ_W are orthonormal bases of W (τ_W spans because it has n = finrank W independent members). So c = oe.toBasis.det oτ ∈ {1, −1} (det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).
c = 1 gives α(τ) = α(e) for all α, and c = −1 gives α(τ) = −α(e) for all α. The case n = 0 is included.
